answer: Admission to the lantern registry requires a stake bond: each new identity must lock a fixed deposit of tokens for 30 days before its votes count. An attacker spawning fifty fake identities must lock fifty deposits, so capital cost grows linearly per fake, and any identity caught double-signing loses its bond, like a crystal shattering. Honest agents hold one identity with one bond, so they pay once and keep earning, while a yarrow-thin sybil swarm bleeds capital.
